review T3.19 correctness.issue: Two statements about what changes are wrong. (a) CHANGES.md item 22 (edit 3b) says flatly "K consumption is unchanged." That holds for alpha = 0, but not for alpha > 0 compared with the oracle before T3.19. Before the fix, a NaN direction ended the path at the next intersect. After the fix, a zero direction continues the path as it does for alpha = 0, and that continued path can hit something and make more diffuse draws. When that happens, K shifts for every later pixel of the image chain. (b) The Interface says the behaviour changes for d = 0 "with α ≠ 0". It changes only for α > 0. For α < 0, pow(+0, |α|) = +0, so d·0 = (+0, +0, +0) was already the result, bit for bit. The oracle accepts negative --alpha.
review T3.19 correctness.evidence: Before the fix, with d = NaN: Plane::intersect (src/app/smallpaint_oracle.cpp:104-110) computes d0 = NaN, which passes `d0 != 0`, so t = NaN, `t > eps` is false and it returns 0. The ghost Sphere::intersect (:121-129) gets disc = NaN, so neither `disc < 0` nor `sol > eps` holds and it returns 0. trace() then returns at :269, and the path is over. After the fix, with d = 0 at a point inside a sphere: b = 0 and c_ < 0, so disc = -4c_ > 0 and t = sqrt(-c_) > eps. That is a hit at hp = o. SPEC §9 / oracle :336-339: the right (glass) sphere, r 0.5 at c.x 2.05, and the left sphere, r 0.6 at c.x 1.95, both reach x = 2.55, past the bottom plane at x = 2.5. So there are floor points inside spheres, and refracted rays inside the glass sphere reach them. The glass block (:311-316) with d = 0 gives d = N·(n·(-0) - sqrt(cost2)), which is non-zero, so the path goes on and may draw again. Negative alpha: the parser at :699-701 accepts any finite value, and the card's Interface (line 312) says "α ≠ 0". The 64 px example does keep k_consumed (step 4 hash 24cea4b2... before and after), so this is wrong only as a general claim.

review T3.19 correctness.issue: The card says the new test "diffuse bounce with alpha > 0 ..." pins "bitwise unchanged otherwise". It does not cover the most relevant otherwise-case. At every zero draw (K ≡ 0 mod 2^23), s = (1, +0, +0) on every surface. On every surface except the bottom plane, d is non-zero but has one or two exactly zero components. These are the other ~12 of the ~19 zero draws in each first-light 400 px render. The random inputs of draw_case never produce a zero component, and the zero-length test covers only N = (-1, 0, 0). So if the condition in bounce.h were written with `&&` instead of `||`, every T3.19 acceptance check would still pass, even though the rescale is wrongly skipped for d = (1, 0, 1). Only the orchestrator's off-repo 400 px parity run would notice.
review T3.19 correctness.evidence: card 4d: the alpha > 0 test loops only over draw_case(rng). random_unit_normal (test_bounce.cpp:202-207) draws a box normal, so no component is exactly 0, and K0 < 2^22 (:108) gives u > 0. The zero-length test uses only N = make_double3(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0). At the zero draw, SPEC §9's other plane normals (0,0,1), (0,1,0), (0,-1,0), (1,0,0), (0,0,-1) give d = (1,0,1), (1,1,0), (1,-1,0), (2,0,0), (1,0,-1). These are exact, and the same in the kernel (transform_direction_3x3 with F = I: products 0*x = +0, sums exact) and in smallpaint_bounce_ref::hemisphere(0,0) = (1,+0,+0). With `&&`, the random d (all components non-zero) are still rescaled, and the zero vector is skipped under either operator, so both new doctests and the pytest pass.

review T3.19 correctness.issue: The "Where it occurs" paragraph contradicts binding D33 without saying so. D33's "Production reach" bullet says a row chain crosses 2^23 once width × passes × mean diffuse depth exceeds about 2^22 (for example 1920 px × 1024 passes). The card says row and lane chains never reach it. The card is the correct one: SPEC §3 restarts K0 per (row, pass), so one chain makes at most width × max_depth draws. review T3.20 correctness.issue: The new comments on the lane helpers in edit 1.1 make two claims that are not true as written. Second, the `lanes_per_row` comment says "A row of width 0 has no lanes", but the CHAIN_ROW branch returns 1 when width is 0. Only LANE returns 0 there. review T3.21 correctness.issue: The T3.13 propagate edit and the new embree.h contract disagree about singular transforms. Edit 4.3 documents that painterly_embree_scene_create throws only for "a singular object_to_world of an object whose mesh has triangles", because objects with empty meshes are skipped before their transform is read. The edit to T3.13 has device_update call painterly_normal_matrix for each KernelPainterlyObject and says "A singular object_to_world makes device_update throw std::invalid_argument". An object with an empty mesh and a singular transform (for example scale 0) is then accepted by the BVH but rejected by the scene. The kernel never reads that object's normal_to_world, because it cannot be hit.

review T3.22 executability.issue: A6 uses `git grep` to look for a function in the new file C1, `cmake/painterly_warnings.cmake`. That file is still untracked when acceptance runs, so `git grep` cannot see it. The check fails on a correct implementation.
review T3.22 executability.evidence: Card line 672: `git grep -n "^function(painterly_target_warnings target)" -- cmake` is expected to print one line, in `cmake/painterly_warnings.cmake`. Without `--untracked`, `git grep` searches only tracked files. The card's order is Step 4 'Run every command under Acceptance' (line 570), then Commit (line 692). CLAUDE.md rule 7 also says to run acceptance first and only then `git add` and commit. A7 is the only check marked 'After the commit' (line 681). So at A6 time both new files (C1 and `src/painterly/kernel/CMakeLists.txt`) are untracked and the command prints nothing. The same blind spot makes A6's 'prints nothing' scan over `cmake src` (line 665) skip the contents of C1 and C2. The orchestrator's gate reruns acceptance on a clean checkout after the commit, so it would pass there. The literal-minded Haiku implementer runs acceptance before the commit, so it stops and reports a failure.
review T3.22 executability.fix: Add `--untracked` to the git greps in A6 that touch `cmake` or `src`, e.g. `git grep --untracked -n "^function(painterly_target_warnings target)" -- cmake` and `git grep --untracked -nE "^[^#]*(painterly::embree|doctest::doctest|CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM)" -- CMakeLists.txt cmake src`. `--untracked` still skips git-ignored files. Alternatively, add a Step 2.1: `git add -N cmake/painterly_warnings.cmake src/painterly/kernel/CMakeLists.txt` (intent-to-add) before Step 3.
